diffuseAlbedo.source: Palette.json: accent.earthenware-sancai ; assets/reference/chinese-ref-sancai-horse.jpg, the collection's reference photograph of this work (assets/reference/CREDITS.md: 'Caparisoned horse', Shaanxi or Henan province, China, Tang dynasty, 675-750, earthenware with sancai glaze, Portland Art Museum, gallery photograph by Daderot, public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Caparisoned_horse,_Shaanxi_or_Henan_province,_China,_Tang_dynasty,_675-750_AD,_earthenware_with_sancai_glaze_-_Portland_Art_Museum_-_Portland,_Oregon_-_DSC08396.jpg ), read 2026-09-27 ; second witness: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 'Horse', Tang dynasty, 1991.253.12 (public domain), https://images.metmuseum.org/CRDImages/as/web-large/1991_253_12.jpg ; J. Y. Shen, J. Henderson, J. Evans, S. Chenery and F. Y. Zhao, 'A study of the glazing techniques and provenances of Tang sancai glazes using elemental and lead isotope analyses', Archaeometry 61, 2 (2019) 358-373, doi:10.1111/arcm.12436, https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/522694/1/Shen_et_al-2019-Archaeometry.pdf
diffuseAlbedo.note: The amber lead glaze, coloured by iron (FeO 1.09 to 5.35 wt.% in Shen et al.'s brown glazes), the horse's dominant glaze: its body, neck and legs are amber-brown, running from orange on the lit chest to Shen et al.'s dark brown on the neck. Read as the mean sRGB of lit patches of the reference (a 1024 x 728 JPEG, taken as sRGB under D65; the photographer's white balance, which leaves the white plinth under the horse near neutral at (65.3, -1.2, 5.5), and exposure, uncalibrated), pixel boxes x0-x1 by y0-y1, converted to CIELAB: the chest 375-420 by 365-400 (36.6, 32.9, 40.1), the hindquarter between the drips 640-655 by 300-345 (36.2, 20.7, 25.1) and 700-720 by 310-345 (32.0, 19.0, 21.0), the flank under the saddle cloth 655-685 by 380-410 (25.6, 24.3, 24.5) and the neck 300-340 by 150-200 (21.9, 19.1, 18.6); the mean of their 5,850 pixels (29.3, 23.8, 26.7), rounded. The Met's horse 1991.253.12 is a cream horse with an amber saddle, whose pale amber (about L* 54) is not this horse's. Its sisters are glaze.sancai-green and glaze.sancai-clear.

refractiveIndex.source: Council Directive 69/493/EEC on crystal glass, Annex I (lead crystal: PbO at least 24 %, refractive index nD at least 1.545), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=celex:31969L0493 ; Wikipedia, 'Lead glass' (ordinary glass 1.5, lead brings it to 1.7 to 1.8; the first Chinese and Roman lead glazes 45-60 % PbO), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_glass
refractiveIndex.note: A lead silicate glass: its index rises with its lead, from at least 1.545 at 24 % PbO (the directive's lead crystal) towards 1.7 to 1.8. Shen et al.'s sancai glazes carry 39.45 to 64.34 wt.% PbO (Table 1), so the index lies between; 1.65 is taken inside that bracket, not measured.

porosity.source: MuseeVision/Docs/Matter/Story.md, 'Glazed stoneware and fired clay' (after Kingery, Bowen and Uhlmann 1976)
porosity.note: The glaze is a glass with no open pores, as the other glazes.

wettingDepth.source: MuseeVision/Docs/Matter/Story.md (a glaze has no open pores)
wettingDepth.derivation: With no open pores, water cannot enter, so the wetting depth is zero.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows.

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
